sections.html:
Find the Register of Deeds at 355 N. Belvedere Drive, Suite 201, Gallatin, TN 37066, by phone at 615-452-3892 or by fax at 615-442-1105. Counter hours are Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 4:30.

One stop covers a lot: the Assessor of Property (Room 206) and the Trustee (Room 107) work in the same building, so a parcel's value and tax status can be checked on the way to or from recording.

In a typical fiscal year the office records more than 30,000 legal documents across over eighty types of instrument (see the county page), so routine home sales are familiar work for the staff.

Eight cities make up Sumner County, which lies about 25 miles northeast of Nashville: Gallatin (the county seat), Hendersonville, Goodlettsville, Millersville, Mitchellville, Portland, Westmoreland and White House. Population was 215,538 in July 2025, a 9.8% gain over April 2020, spread over 89,138 housing units of which 72.0% are owner-occupied. Median value of an owner-occupied home is $393,100 for 2020 to 2024, owners carrying a mortgage pay a median $1,831 monthly, and 3,045 building permits were issued in 2025. With prices at that level, the state transfer tax is a meaningful line on a closing statement, so have your title company total it early.

Online records, searchable at ustitlesearch.net, are certified from September 1989 forward. The deed books and indexes reach back to 1786 in digitized form, which lets you trace an older chain of title from home. If you prefer, a public search room is open at the office.

MyLandAlert is a free fraud monitor the register operates with ProGResS, Inc. It sends an email whenever a document is recorded under your name or business, giving you early warning of a forged deed or mortgage fraud. Owners of rentals, vacant lots and inherited houses benefit most.

The office accepts e-recorded deeds through Simplifile, Inc. and CSC eRecording Solutions, and documents are received, recorded and returned faster than with paper. Tennessee restricts electronic submission to professionals such as attorneys, lenders and title companies, so a seller typically depends on whoever is handling the sale.

Paper still works. File in person or by mail at Suite 201 with the original signed, notarized deed and the fees. Because fees depend on the document, call 615-452-3892 for the exact recording fee before you send it.

At recording the register collects the state transfer tax and mortgage tax in addition to the recording fees. The state taxes are forwarded to the Department of Revenue monthly, and the county retains the recording fees. State rates:

State recordation taxes collected at the register
TaxRate
Realty transfer tax$0.37 per $100 of purchase price
Mortgage tax$0.115 per $100 of debt, first $2,000 exempt

Your purchase contract says who covers the tax. Some transfers owe none under state law, including an executor's deed under a will and a divorce settlement deed. A buyer's new loan puts the mortgage tax on the lender's deed of trust, and the release for your old loan is recorded after closing.

Tennessee Code dictates what a recordable deed contains. The usual list:

  • Names of grantor and grantee, with a legal description
  • Derivation clause that names the earlier recorded deed
  • Name and address of the owner and the tax payer, and of the preparer
  • Parcel number, plus a sworn statement of value if the deed is taxable
  • Notarized acknowledgment of the signature

Staff do not draft documents or give legal advice, and a deed missing an item can be turned away. Your closing attorney or title company normally runs through this list for you.

sections.h2: What to bring to the counter
sections.html:
Bring the signed, notarized original deed and payment covering both recording and any state tax. When a lender is involved, the title company usually submits the deed of trust alongside it. Note three details beforehand, because the deed needs all of them: the parcel number from the Assessor's records, the recording reference of the prior deed, and the mailing address for the tax bill.

Once recorded, the document is scanned into the database and can be viewed online. File the recorded copy with your closing papers, since lenders and buyers sometimes ask later for the instrument number. If something looks wrong on the recorded copy, such as a misspelled name or a wrong parcel number, tell your closing agent right away so a corrective document can be prepared and recorded.

sections.h2: Step by step for a seller
sections.html:
Most sales follow the same path through this office. Your title company or attorney prepares the deed and checks it against the list above. You sign before a notary, and the original goes to the register either by e-recording or on paper at Suite 201. The register's staff index the deed, collect the state tax and the recording fees, and add the document to the database.

Fees are modest next to the tax. The county keeps the recording fees, while the state transfer tax and any mortgage tax are passed to the Department of Revenue each month. If you are selling a house you inherited, or one that was part of a divorce or a will, ask whether the transfer qualifies as one of the no-tax types before the deed is drawn, because that changes what the closing agent collects.

Call 615-452-3892 if you are unsure whether a document can be recorded as it stands. Asking before you mail the packet is cheaper than having it returned.

sections.h2: Is the house really in Sumner County?
sections.html: Not always. Part of Goodlettsville is in Davidson County, and Millersville, Portland and White House each extend into Robertson County, so a Sumner city in the mailing address does not prove the parcel is in Sumner County. Check the Assessor's property search or the deed's parcel number before you pick a register's office, and ask the title company which county gets the filing.

A recorded deed changes the owner of record and settles no tax. County taxes are due the first Monday in October and become delinquent after February 28. Before closing, get the parcel balance from the Trustee at 615-452-1260, and let the Assessor at 615-452-2412 know where the new owner wants the bill sent.

Work out the sequence with your closing agent: confirm the balance, sign and notarize the deed, file it, and wait for the scan to appear in the database. A cash buyer needs no deed of trust and owes no mortgage tax, so the packet is shorter and there is one less document to follow.

faqs.q: What are the Sumner County Register of Deeds hours?
faqs.a: Weekdays from 8:00 until 4:30, at 355 N. Belvedere Drive, Suite 201, Gallatin. The phone is 615-452-3892.
Yes, through Simplifile, Inc. and CSC eRecording Solutions. Most sellers let a title company with an existing account do it.

faqs.q: How far back do Sumner County online records go?
faqs.a: Certified records start in September 1989 and are searchable online, and digitized deed books and indexes reach back to 1786.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax on a Sumner County sale?
faqs.a: The state rate is $0.37 per $100 of purchase price, collected when the deed is recorded. Ask your title company for the total on your sale.

faqs.q: Can I get alerts about filings under my name in Sumner County?
faqs.a: Yes, sign up for MyLandAlert. It is free and emails you when a document is recorded under your name or business.
